lines.text: For sixteen years, the internet has argued about one question.
Did the top fall?
It's the wrong question.
Tonight, we retell Inception, with one single change.
What if Mal was right?
Dom Cobb washes up on a beach, below a castle he has never seen before.
Cobb is a thief. But he doesn't break into buildings. He breaks into dreams.
Inside, at a long golden table, he is pitching a billionaire named Saito.
Your mind is a vault. I can teach you to guard it.
It's a con. While Saito sleeps, Cobb is already cracking the safe inside his head.
But someone keeps showing up to wreck the job. His wife. Mal.
You know this isn't real, Dom.
The dream collapses. The castle floods. And Saito wakes up, impressed.
Saito doesn't want revenge. He wants to hire him.
Don't steal an idea. Plant one. Inception.
The target is Robert Fischer, heir to an energy empire. The idea: break up your father's company.
The payment is the only thing Cobb wants. One phone call, and he can go home to his children.
Children whose faces he can never quite see. Remember that.
So Cobb builds a team.
In Paris, he finds Ariadne, an architect who folds an entire city over their heads on her first try.
Arthur, the point man, who plans for everything.
Eames, a forger in Mombasa, who can wear any face.
And Yusuf, a chemist, whose sedative lets them go three dreams deep.
A dream, inside a dream, inside a dream. And time stretches. Ten hours on a plane becomes a week, then six months, then ten years.
But Ariadne discovers what Cobb is hiding.
Deep in his mind, there is an elevator. Every floor is a memory of Mal. He visits her every night.
You promised we would grow old together.
And wherever Cobb goes, she follows.
The job begins on a ten hour flight. One drink, and Fischer is under.
Level one. A rainy city. And immediately, everything goes wrong.
A freight train tears down the middle of the street. Fischer's mind has been trained. His subconscious has an army.
Saito is hit. And under this sedative, dying doesn't wake you up. It drops you into limbo. An endless dream, where decades pass in minutes.
There's no way out but down. Yusuf drives. The rest go deeper.
Level two. A hotel. Cobb tells Fischer the truth: you are dreaming. Then lies about everything else.
Above them, the van swerves, and gravity goes with it. Arthur fights a guard down a spinning hallway.
Level three. A fortress in the snow, with Fischer's father locked in a vault at its heart.
They are seconds from the door, when Mal steps out of the shadows. And Fischer falls.
The job is dead. Unless Cobb follows him. All the way down.
Limbo. An ocean, and a city crumbling into it. Cobb knows this place. He and Mal built it.
They spent fifty years here. They grew old here. And Mal forgot it was a dream.
So Cobb did something unforgivable. He found the safe in her mind, and planted one small idea.
Your world is not real.
It worked. They woke up. But the idea kept growing. Back in the real world, she still believed she was dreaming. And one night, she took the leap, to wake up.
That is the movie you know. In that movie, Cobb lets her go, saves Saito, and walks through an airport to his kids.
Here is where we change it.

chapters.card: CHAPTER SEVEN|WHAT IF MAL WAS RIGHT?

lines.text: In our version, Mal doesn't fight him. She asks him one question.
Why can you never see their faces?
And Cobb has no answer.
Because you have never seen them this old. I have.
Mal didn't die that night. She woke up. Cobb is the one who stayed asleep.
For years, she has sat beside him, building dream after dream, trying to reach him.
Saito. The crew. The heist. Every one of them was hers.
Fischer was never the target. Cobb was. And the idea she came to plant is the simplest one in the world.
Come home.
The kicks fire. The fortress falls. The hotel drops. The van hits the water.
Cobb wakes on the plane. Walks through the airport. Opens his front door.
The children turn around. And for the first time, he sees their faces.
He spins the top. And in the original, he walks away.
In ours, he stays. He watches. And it does not fall.
So he sits down. Leans back. And lets go.
He opens his eyes in a quiet room. Grey hair. And a hand, holding his.
Welcome back.
Two grown children are standing in the doorway.
And on the table beside the bed, a small metal top wobbles, and falls.
At least, that one does.
So. Was Mal right all along? Comment fall, or spin.
And tell us which movie we should reimagine next.
Titanic, where the door fits two? The Matrix, where Neo takes the blue pill? Or Interstellar, where Cooper never leaves?
The top comment gets made. And send this to the friend who still swears the top fell.
